name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_MCQ_Q19 - Identifying C1-C4 and C1-C6 glycosidic linkages in glucose dimers

questiontext.text: Three structures are given below in which two glucose units are linked. Which of these linkages between glucose units are between C1 and C4 and which linkages are between C1 and C6?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Three disaccharide structures labeled (I), (II), and (III) are shown, each composed of two \(\alpha\)-D-glucopyranose units joined by an oxygen bridge labeled (A), (B), and (C), respectively.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
In the standard Haworth projection of D-glucopyranose (with the ring oxygen at the upper right and the \(-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}\) group at the upper left), the ring carbons are numbered clockwise starting from the rightmost carbon adjacent to the ring oxygen as \(\text{C}1\), followed by \(\text{C}2\) (bottom right), \(\text{C}3\) (bottom left), \(\text{C}4\) (leftmost), \(\text{C}5\) (upper left, bearing the exocyclic carbon), and the exocyclic \(-\text{CH}_2-\) group as \(\text{C}6\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
A glycosidic linkage between \(\text{C}1\) and \(\text{C}4\) joins the anomeric carbon (\(\text{C}1\)) of one glucose unit directly to the ring carbon \(\text{C}4\) of the second unit, whereas a \(\text{C}1\text{--}\text{C}6\) linkage joins \(\text{C}1\) of one unit to the exocyclic \(-\text{CH}_2-\) carbon (\(\text{C}6\)) of the second unit.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
In structure (I), the oxygen bridge (A) connects \(\text{C}1\) of the left glucopyranose ring to \(\text{C}4\) of the right glucopyranose ring, forming a \(\text{C}1\text{--}\text{C}4\) linkage. In structure (II), the oxygen bridge (B) connects \(\text{C}1\) of the upper glucopyranose ring to the exocyclic \(-\text{CH}_2-\) carbon (\(\text{C}6\)) of the lower glucopyranose ring, forming a \(\text{C}1\text{--}\text{C}6\) linkage. In structure (III), the oxygen bridge (C) connects \(\text{C}1\) of the lower-left glucopyranose ring to \(\text{C}4\) of the upper-right glucopyranose ring, forming a \(\text{C}1\text{--}\text{C}4\) linkage.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Thus, (A) and (C) are between \(\text{C}1\) and \(\text{C}4\), while (B) is between \(\text{C}1\) and \(\text{C}6\).

answer.text: (A) is between C1 and C4, (B) and (C) are between C1 and C6
(A) and (B) are between C1 and C4, (C) is between C1 and C6
(A) and (C) are between C1 and C4, (B) is between C1 and C6
(A) and (C) are between C1 and C6, (B) is between C1 and C4
